rows.question: What concrete regulatory decision must the analysis support, at what level and on what date?
rows.basis: SIENNA scoping; distinguish technology, artefact and application; avoid pitching the analysis too high in the technology stack.
rows.operationalisation: Fix the ADS/FAV use case, jurisdiction, legal snapshot date, ODD, test/deployment status, passenger/goods/service context and the precise decision to be supported.
rows.checks: Vehicle vs ADS vs service/system; public-road use; testing vs ordinary deployment; commercial vs non-commercial use.
rows.rule: Do not code or diagnose gaps before the object and legal time-slice are fixed.
rows.title: Decision question & scope

rows.question: Which features, functions and affordances of the technology matter legally and socially?
rows.basis: Essential characteristics, salient features and affordances; intended function and users; who drives the technology; interests and business model.
rows.operationalisation: Map DDT, fallback/MRM, ODD, remote management/intervention, control-centre functions, data/logging, updates, cybersecurity, service organisation and lifecycle dependencies.
rows.checks: Absence/change of human driver; remote functions; ODD limits; software/update lifecycle; system/service dependencies.
rows.rule: Regulate the relevant practice and sociotechnical context, not merely the label attached to the technology.
rows.title: Sociotechnical mapping

rows.question: What is the problem represented to be, by whom, and what alternative frames exist?
rows.basis: Problem frames reflect roles, interests, values, information and implicit assumptions; separate problem definition from solution.
rows.operationalisation: Record competing frames before legal conclusions: safety, market access, innovation, road access, liability, labour, privacy/data, cybersecurity, local impacts and cross-border operation.
rows.rule: A preferred solution is not evidence that the problem was correctly framed.
rows.title: Problem framing

rows.question: Who benefits, who bears risk or cost, and which rights/values are affected?
rows.basis: SIENNA ethical assessment: scope; stratify; describe; identify impacts/stakeholders; identify and analyse ethical issues; evaluate/recommend.
rows.operationalisation: Map direct/indirect benefits and harms, distributional effects and vulnerable groups; distinguish empirical risk from normative conflict.
rows.checks: Safety, responsibility, privacy/surveillance, employment, autonomy/de-skilling, cybersecurity, market/data power, accessibility and vulnerable road users.
rows.rule: Stakeholder salience informs the analysis but does not by itself determine the legal outcome.
rows.title: Stakeholders, impacts & ethics

rows.question: What law already applies before assuming that new AV-specific law is needed?
rows.basis: SIENNA legal method: scope; identify legal issues; analyse international/regional/national norms; identify gaps/challenges.
rows.operationalisation: Map international/UNECE, EU, national and where relevant local/private/standards layers; search by legal function/category, not only by technology name.
rows.asset: Intelligence Register; ROAT Regulatory Map; Public Library
rows.checks: Vienna Convention/WP.1; UNECE/WP.29; EU type approval; national road traffic/testing/operator rules; liability/insurance; AI/data/cybersecurity; standards/guidance.
rows.rule: An apparent lacuna may disappear once inherited general law and adjacent regulatory layers are examined.
rows.title: Multi-level legal landscape

rows.question: How deeply is automated driving legally embedded in each regulatory function?
rows.basis: TechReg provides the wider process; the N0–N4 vector is a ROAT-specific empirical module.
rows.operationalisation: Code technical approval; road access/operation; actor allocation; liability/risk; behavioural rules; infrastructure; international/cross-border recognition. Record evidence, rationale, confidence and caveat.
rows.asset: Layer Coding – AV History; Cross-section 2026 – AV Normalisation
rows.checks: Separate mature type approval from lawful road/service deployment; do not collapse operator, user, ADS and remote roles.
rows.rule: Scores measure legal embedding, not regulatory intensity. Layer range is a descriptive asymmetry signal, not a statistical index.
rows.title: ROAT functional-layer coding

rows.question: Where and how does the fit between law and sociotechnical practice break?
rows.basis: Descriptive disconnect; normative disconnect; business/use-model disconnect. Downstream symptoms include need for special law, uncertainty, over-/under-inclusiveness and obsolescence.
rows.operationalisation: Classify each alleged gap. Distinguish true lacuna from interpretive uncertainty, implementation gap, enforcement deficit, unintended effect or obsolete premise.
rows.checks: Driver-based definitions; testing rules used for deployment; actor-role mismatch; commercial-use assumptions; outdated human-control premises.
rows.rule: A genuinely normative disconnect may require legislative choice rather than aggressive interpretation.
rows.title: Disconnect / gap diagnosis

rows.question: What legal mechanism lets one regulatory layer function while adjacent layers remain less mature?
rows.basis: TechReg moves from gap analysis to intervention; ROAT adds an AV-specific bridge/gate taxonomy for asynchronous legal embedding.
rows.operationalisation: Identify deeming, equivalence/exemption, conditional permits, safety cases, service-level validation, operator licensing, mutual recognition, transitional rules and other bridges/gates.
rows.asset: Layer Coding – AV History; Cross-section 2026 – AV Normalisation
rows.checks: Article 34bis; Article 39/equivalence; national testing permits; France safety-case/mise-en-service; Croatia service validation; GB staged permits.
rows.rule: A bridge manages inter-layer mismatch; it does not by itself prove full regulatory normalisation.
rows.title: Bridge / gate analysis

rows.question: Why intervene, whose interests are served, and what stance toward innovation is justified?
rows.basis: Market failure; public interests/rights; SHEC rationales; private-interest/capture critique. Innovation governance: precaution, permissionless innovation, responsible innovation, innovation principle.
rows.operationalisation: Test necessity, proportionality, distributional effects, capture risk, uncertainty, reversibility, observability and capacity to learn through monitored deployment.
rows.checks: Safety benefits and residual risk; market access; learning-by-testing; irreversible physical harm; regulatory cost; incumbent/new-entrant interests.
rows.rule: Reject the shortcut ‘new technology = new law’. The intervention needs an independent justification.
rows.title: Justification & innovation posture

rows.question: Who or what should be regulated, with which instrument, and how will the control loop work?
rows.basis: Rules/principles/standards; 8 Cs: command, competition, consensus, communication, contract, claims, code, compensation. Control loop: standard-setting, monitoring, behaviour modification/enforcement.
rows.operationalisation: Allocate obligations to the correct actor/function; combine public law, technical requirements, licences/permits, standards, contractual allocation, disclosure, code/design and insurance/compensation where appropriate.
rows.asset: Draft Legislative Architecture; Amendment Draft – CPT 1329; Roles & Concepts
rows.checks: Type approval; operator/service authorisation; control-centre duties; remote-management constraints; incident/in-use reporting; sanctions; insurance/compensation; software/update controls.
rows.rule: Always identify who sets the standard, who monitors compliance and who can impose or trigger corrective action.
rows.title: Regulatory design & instruments

rows.question: Is the intervention legally valid, institutionally legitimate, accountable and likely to be accepted?
rows.basis: Legality is distinct from legitimacy. Legitimacy has input, throughput and output dimensions; acceptance is the sociological question whether regulatees treat the rule as binding; accountability sustains legitimacy.
rows.operationalisation: Check legal basis/competence, procedure, participation, transparency, review/appeal, consistency, effectiveness, accountability forum and expected compliance/acceptance.
rows.asset: Draft Legislative Architecture; Amendment Draft – CPT 1329
rows.checks: Ministerial competence; EU/national competence boundary; consultation/notification; authority discretion; review rights; proportional burden on operators/users.
rows.rule: Legal validity does not establish legitimacy; formal compliance does not establish normative acceptance.
rows.title: Legality, legitimacy, acceptance & accountability

rows.question: What regulatory configuration/pathway does the jurisdiction represent, and what can travel across borders?
rows.basis: TechReg is general; ROAT adds comparative vector/pathway analysis to test how different legal systems sequence normalisation.
rows.operationalisation: Compare layer vectors, leading/lagging functions, bridge/gate forms, institutional design and portability of safety evidence/approvals.
rows.asset: Cross-section 2026 – AV Normalisation; Layer Coding – AV History
rows.checks: Technical/harmonisation-first; actor/institutional-first; deployment-assurance; testing-permit pathways; cross-border recognition of evidence and operation.
rows.rule: Do not force jurisdictions onto a single linear ladder; configurations may have different leading layers.
rows.title: Comparative pathway & portability

rows.question: What post-deployment evidence can falsify assumptions and trigger revision?
rows.basis: TechReg is iterative; the Chapter 9 control loop and Chapter 10 failure analysis imply continuous monitoring, adjustment and accountability.
rows.operationalisation: Define review triggers around incidents, in-use safety, ODD changes, software updates, cybersecurity, remote-management performance, enforcement outcomes and material service changes.
rows.asset: Monitoring Watchlist; Intelligence Register; Safety/remote-management records
rows.checks: SMS/in-use reporting; incidents/near misses; update governance; retraining/retesting; change control; operational data and enforcement feedback.
rows.rule: Monitoring is part of the regulatory architecture, not merely research administration; evidence must feed back into earlier stages.
rows.title: In-use monitoring & iteration

verdict.label: Keep from ROAT
verdict.what: N0–N4 functional-layer vector; actor/function ontology; bridge/gate analysis; pathway families; explicit evidence, confidence and caveat discipline.
verdict.why: These are more granular for automated-vehicle legal architecture than the general TechReg model.
verdict.how: Treat them as the core AV-specific module inside stages 5–8 and 12.
verdict.asset: Layer Coding – AV History; Cross-section 2026; Roles & Concepts
verdict.caveat: ROAT’s distinctive contribution is layered/asynchronous normalisation and the bridge/gate mechanism.

verdict.label: Add from Leenes
verdict.what: Sociotechnical scoping; problem framing; stakeholder/ethical assessment; explicit justification for intervention; innovation-governance posture; instrument choice/control loop; legality–legitimacy–acceptance–accountability.
verdict.why: These supply the upstream and downstream stages that were less explicit in the current ROAT analytical architecture.
verdict.how: Use them as mandatory questions, with depth proportionate to the task.
verdict.caveat: Depth should follow the decision question, not a fixed page count.

verdict.label: Keep separate
verdict.what: Operational Hub Methodology and substantive regulatory-analysis methodology solve different problems.
verdict.why: The existing Methodology tab governs evidence/workflow integrity, not the substance of AV regulatory analysis.
verdict.how: Do not overwrite the operational Methodology tab; use this dedicated analytical tab.
verdict.caveat: Maintain bidirectional source/output integrity independently of the analytical framework.

verdict.label: Recommended pilot
verdict.what: Run one end-to-end case to test whether the framework generates additional decision-relevant insight without making ordinary analyses unnecessarily complex.
verdict.why: The framework is expressly designed to be iterative and scalable from quick scan to deep analysis.
verdict.how: Pilot on the Slovakia transition from conditional/test operation toward ordinary/commercial FAV deployment, then compare the result with France and Croatia.
verdict.caveat: If added stages do not change decisions or expose hidden assumptions, simplify them rather than expanding the framework for its own sake.

intro: ROAT Regulatory Analysis Framework – TechReg integration

Core principle: use Leenes’ TechReg model as the outer iterative regulatory-governance process; retain the ROAT N0–N4 functional-layer model, actor ontology and bridge/gate analysis as the automated-vehicle-specific legal architecture module. Later findings may require reframing earlier stages.
